transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-05-12 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Recorded: yes (auto)
- Attendees: Sofia Morales (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (NovaSearch Head of Search), Ethan Rivers (ML Engineer), Priya Singh (Product)

Summary:
Short demo of Redwood Hosted API focusing on embeddings + reranking as a search relevance workflow. Walked through embedding endpoints, similarity search patterns, and the rerank endpoint flow (embed -> candidate retrieve -> rerank). Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, caching, VPC/tenant isolation (they are hosted-first but sensitive to data residency), and next steps for POC data handoff and benchmark.

Topics Covered:
- Hosted embeddings endpoint (API usage, batch vs streaming)
- Candidate retrieval patterns and vector DB integrations (Pinecone mention)
- Redwood rerank endpoint + structured output support
- Console demo: per-route latency/cost, token breakdown, rollouts
- Optimize suggestions: batching, quantization, prefix caching
- Security briefly: SOC 2, encryption, KMS, RBAC

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Okay hi everyone thanks for joining, I'm Sofia with Redwood, and Liam's our solutions engineer today. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Maya: Good thanks. excited to see the embeddings flow, we're exploring replacing part of our pipeline that's currently on Elastic and some Pinecone experiments.
[00:15] Liam: Awesome. Quick agenda: we'll demo the hosted embeddings endpoint, show candidate retrieval patterns, then do a rerank walkthrough and the console for observability and Optimize recommendations.
[00:25] Ethan: Quick question up front — our main constraint is 200ms p95 on search hits end-to-end, is that realistic with hosted?
[00:32] Liam: Yeah so depends on topology. For pure embed+vector DB retrieval then a lightweight rerank, you can hit that with low-latency zones. We'll show how caching and prefix KV cache reduces repeated token cost and latency; hosted has region routing and bursts.
[00:45] Priya: Also curious about data retention — we cannot have customer PII stored long-term, what's Redwood's default?
[00:52] Sofia: By default hosted retains logs for 30 days but we have customer options and strict retention policies, and enterprise contracts can set no-retention or VPC private deployment. We'll share the SOC 2 and security pack after this.
[01:05] [Liam screenshares a quick curl demo]
[01:10] Liam: Here's a simple embeddings call, same as in the docs: POST /v1/embeddings with model param, you get a vector back. We demo batching — e.g., send 50 sentences in one call.
[01:22] Maya: what's the typical vector size for recommended models?
[01:25] Liam: often 1536 for the medium family, we also have 1024 and 4096 variants depending on model. For rerank we recommend the 1536 tradeoff. Becker? — sorry, bad name, um — our docs list common sizes. (slight laugh)
[01:40] Ethan: Are we expected to store embeddings in our own vector DB or can Redwood handle that?
[01:45] Sofia: Two patterns: you can host embeddings in your vector DB (Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate), or use Redwood's managed candidate store for quick POCs. For enterprise we often see customers keep vectors in their own infra for residency.
[01:58] Liam: Now the rerank flow: we take user query, embed it, retrieve ~100 candidates via approximate NN, then call Redwood /v1/rerank with query + candidates; rerank uses a cross-encoder-ish model to score. The endpoint supports structured output so you can get scores and explanations in JSON.
[02:16] Priya: Can rerank run in <100ms?
[02:20] Liam: For small candidate sets and optimized models yes — typically 60-150ms depending on sequence lengths and model choice. There's a tradeoff with cost. Our Optimize recommendations will tune batch sizes and quantization to bring cost down while keeping p95 under target.
[02:35] Maya: show us the console? we want to see cost per route and token breakdown.
[02:40] Liam: sure. [screen share: Redwood Console] Here is the per-model dashboard, token-level cost, latency histogram, and per-route traces. You can set rollout policies and canary for models; if latency spikes we have automatic fallback to a cheaper compat model.
[03:05] Ethan: typo in one of the traces — looks like K V cache spelled odd in logs?
[03:09] Liam: Yeah internal auto transcription of logs sometimes breaks but the runtime uses KV cache for incremental decoding — reduces repeated compute on chat-style workloads.
[03:18] Maya: security question: Can we use our KMS for key management if we do private?
[03:22] Sofia: Yes, for Private deployments and VPC we integrate with customer KMS/HSM — we'll include the architecture doc.
[03:30] [Liam runs a live rerank demo with sample queries]
[03:35] Liam: Example query: "how do I reset password". We retrieve candidates from their vector DB (simulated) then call rerank; you can set explain:true to get token-level rationales — which is helpful for debugging.
[03:50] Maya: that's really helpful. Our product team wants to see how rerank changes ordering vs our current BM25 baseline.
[03:56] Liam: We recommend running an A/B with a holdout, Redwood supports rollout experiments and evaluation hooks to track NDCG/CTR. Also you can wire in our evals to run periodic regression tests.
[04:10] Priya: integration wise — SDK or direct REST?
[04:13] Sofia: both — we have SDKs in Python/Node, and REST examples in the docs. SDK supports streaming and easier retry logic.
[04:20] Ethan: about vector DB: latency we saw with Pinecone in past — do you have any benchmark pages?
[04:25] Liam: yes we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet; we also run a hosted knn store for low-latency POCs. For production at scale people prefer colocated vector DB + Redwood in same region.
[04:40] [Maya asks about cost model]
[04:43] Sofia: Hosted pricing is per-embedding unit and per-rerank call (token and compute based). We also have reserved options for Dedicated. I'll send a pricing sheet after this.
[04:55] Maya: what about GDPR/data residency?
[04:58] Sofia: We have region controls; hosted can pin region for your tenant and private deployments give full control over data flows. We'll include the compliance sheet.
[05:08] Ethan: any limitations on sequence length for rerank?
[05:11] Liam: Rerank handles typical doc sizes; longer sequences increase latency. We support chunking best practices in the docs.
[05:20] [demo continues — Liam toggles model variants and shows latency/cost delta]
[05:30] Liam: here's an Optimize suggestion — for this workload it recommends lower-precision quantized model for rerank to save ~30% cost with <2% quality delta.
[05:40] Priya: that's compelling.
[05:42] Maya: internal stakeholders — our infra lead wants to know about SSO and audit logs.
[05:47] Sofia: We support SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit logs streamed to your SIEM. We'll include the log schema.
[05:55] Ethan: can we do a short POC — say 2 weeks — to validate relevance improvements?
[05:59] Sofia: Absolutely. Typical POC: provide sample dataset and queries, Redwood team runs rerank bench and we provide a result deck and config suggestions.
[06:10] Maya: timeline: we are aiming for an internal decision in 6 weeks, so a 2-week POC fits.
[06:15] Sofia: Great. Next steps after this call we'll send pricing, security docs, and a trial API key; Liam will run an initial benchmark once you share data.
[06:25] [Participants ask about competitor lock-in]
[06:28] Liam: We try to keep things portable — standard embeddings and exportable vectors so you can keep control over vectors. Our routing supports fallback to compatible model variants so you aren't locked to a single black-box model.
[06:40] Priya: any gotchas with rate limits? we can burst but need predictable throughput.
[06:45] Sofia: For hosted we have quotas, burst policies, and SLA-backed Dedicated for predictable throughput. We'll propose quota tiers in the pricing doc.
[07:00] [Wrap-up — recap and explicit next steps]
[07:05] Sofia: Recap: 1) we'll send pricing + quotas, 2) security pack (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs), 3) trial API key and sandbox project, 4) Liam to run rerank bench when Maya shares data.
[07:20] Maya: thanks all, will share data and eval criteria by Friday.
[07:28] Ethan: appreciate the demo.
[07:30] Sofia: Thanks everyone.
